audit_scope.description: This audit covers both EL and CL logic. EIP-7935 affects EL block production and gas limits. PeerDAS polynomial commitment sampling affects CL data availability. EIP-7600 (Pectra meta) provides context for the pre-Fusaka fork state.

out_of_scope_reasons.JSON-RPC API: Explicitly out-of-scope per Ethereum Bug Bounty — requires publicly exposed API
out_of_scope_reasons.Beacon API: Explicitly out-of-scope per Ethereum Bug Bounty — requires publicly exposed API
out_of_scope_reasons.Configuration: Requires node operator error, not external attack
out_of_scope_reasons.High-effort DoS: Sustained, CPU or bandwidth intensive, and/or requires more than 1 packet or on-chain transaction
out_of_scope_reasons.Non-Fusaka vulnerabilities: Should be submitted via the standard Ethereum Foundation Bug Bounty Program
out_of_scope_reasons.EIP-7600 (Pectra meta): Pectra is a prior fork, not Fusaka-specific. Included for context only.

el_vectors.threat: Submit malformed or resource-exhausting transactions exploiting increased 60M gas limit
Send invalid blocks, adversarial worst-case-size blocks at 60M gas to strain propagation

cl_vectors.threat: Send crafted cells, proofs, or commitments that exploit deserialization or verification bugs in PeerDAS
Propose blocks with invalid blob commitments, withhold cells to degrade data availability

misclassified_entities.reason: The Data Availability Sampler is an internal CL component that collects cells from the network. It is not an external entity — the actual external source is the network peer providing the cells. Reclassified as internal; the trust boundary is at the network peer level.

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Node via P2P Network
trusted_external_entities.rationale: P2P network peers are unauthenticated. Any node can join and send arbitrary protocol messages including crafted cells, proofs, and blocks. All input must be fully validated including BLS subgroup checks, field element range checks, byte length checks, and KZG proof verification.

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Node via devp2p
trusted_external_entities.rationale: EL P2P peers are unauthenticated. Malicious peers can send adversarially constructed blocks maximizing serialized size under the new 60M gas limit, or invalid transactions.

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Sender via JSON-RPC / P2P
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Transaction submission (eth_sendRawTransaction or P2P transaction gossip)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External users submit transactions with arbitrary gas limits. Under EIP-7935 the block gas limit increases to 60M, meaning single transactions could consume significantly more gas. Full transaction validation required including gas limit checks.

trusted_external_entities.name: Consensus Layer via Engine API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Authenticated via JWT. CL sends execution payloads for validation. Content must still be validated — payload may contain blocks up to 60M gas. A compromised or buggy CL could send invalid payloads.

trusted_external_entities.name: Execution Layer via Engine API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Authenticated via JWT. EL returns blob data and execution results to CL. Per bug bounty scope, blob data from engine_getBlobsV2 may be used without KZG verification by CL, meaning corrupted EL data could propagate to the network.

trusted_external_entities.name: Adversarial Block Builder
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Block production (via proposer selection or MEV relay)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: A malicious block builder can construct worst-case blocks that maximize serialized size under 60M gas (e.g., zero-byte-heavy calldata). These blocks must remain within the CL 10 MiB gossip limit to propagate. This is a cross-boundary concern affecting both EL and CL.

trusted_external_entities.name: Blob Producer (Validator/Beacon Node)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Blob producers (validators or beacon nodes) provide raw blob data for encoding into cells. While typically local/trusted, the blob data itself must be validated (length check, polynomial conversion). Blob content is ultimately from user transactions and could be adversarial.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: PeerDAS cell/proof reception via P2P gossip
boundary_edges.security_assumption: All received cells, proofs, and commitments must be validated: byte length checks (BYTES_PER_COMMITMENT, BYTES_PER_PROOF, BYTES_PER_CELL), cell index bounds (< CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB), BLS subgroup checks on deserialized group elements, field element range checks (< BLS_MODULUS), and KZG batch proof verification via pairing check.

Blocks received via gossip must not exceed 10 MiB gossip message size limit. Block content must be fully validated against consensus rules. With 60M gas blocks, worst-case serialized size must be checked.
Full block validation required: gas limit enforcement, transaction validity, state transition correctness. Adversarial blocks may maximize size under 60M gas limit.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Transaction pool ingress (via RPC or P2P gossip)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Full transaction validation required: signature verification, gas limit check (must not exceed block gas limit), nonce validation, balance sufficiency. Per-transaction gas cap enforcement if applicable (EIP-7825 coordination).

JWT authentication verified. Payload content must be independently validated by EL: block gas limit, transaction validity, state root computation. EL must not blindly trust CL-provided execution payloads.

JWT authentication verified. CL should validate blob data returned by EL via KZG verification. Per bug bounty scope notes, some CL implementations may skip KZG verification on engine_getBlobsV2 responses, creating a trust boundary vulnerability if EL is compromised.

Blocks must pass all consensus and execution validation. Worst-case serialized block size at 60M gas must remain below CL 10 MiB gossip limit. Block size validation must be enforced before gossip propagation.
Blob length must equal BYTES_PER_BLOB. Polynomial conversion and cell computation must handle all valid blob contents without panics or overflows.

notes: EXT-DATA-AVAILABILITY-SAMPLER was reclassified as internal (misclassified_entities). Its trust boundary is covered by EXT-PEER-NODE-P2P.
EIP-7600 (Pectra meta) had no external entities and is not Fusaka-specific. Included for completeness but flagged as out-of-scope for Fusaka bug bounty.
EXT-BLOCK-PRODUCER from EIP-7935 gas economics subgraph was merged into the adversarial block builder entity, as the security-relevant scenario is adversarial block construction.
